steps.what: Check solar installation readiness and building inspection requirements with responsible parties
Prepare inspection scheduling request and supporting project details
Check and send request and agree inspection appointment with inspector and site
outputs: agreed inspection appointment or scheduling exception

tasks.design: Configure a reusable inspection request in {PROJECT} using checked project details and document links. The manager checks the exact request, sends it and agrees the appointment; no external booking interface or inspection approval is presumed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Scheduling requests repeat project, access and contact details.
tasks.enabler_now: Native templates can reuse checked information without deciding readiness or booking externally.
tasks.still_hard: Changing readiness, inspector availability and safe site access.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing whether the project is genuinely ready and negotiating a workable visit.
tasks.altitude: Less request preparation; inspection coordination responsibility stays unchanged.

reach.task: Clarify visit prerequisites and required documents
reach.learn: Which missing items prevent an inspection

evidence.claim: Reusable scheduling templates can reduce repeated request preparation; this is an unmeasured design assumption.

assumptions: Boundary is arranging a visit, excluding the inspector's assessment and project remediation.
The manager produces project ID, inspection type, location, contact, access restrictions, readiness and proposed dates in s1; all confirmation and capture time is retained.
Existing project documents come from unchanged project administration; s2 retains selecting documents, template entry and exceptions rather than assuming free structured inputs.
Test native templates first. Missing details or unsupported appointment channels use the current manual route.
s3 retains request checking and all appointment negotiation. Each changed request or appointment proposal requires a fresh human check.
unknowns: Inspection process, native templates and repeated entry burden
research_questions: Can a native template reduce preparation without increasing inspector queries?

already_counted.description: Request completion in s2 and checking/appointment agreement in s3

incremental.description: Maintain request template and contact defaults

approvals.approved_version: Exact request project, inspection type, location, readiness statement, attachments, recipient and proposed appointment; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=30+12+40=82; gross 18 minus 1 upkeep gives net 17. High assumes repeated request fields; low covers variable requirements and scheduling exceptions absorbing the benefit.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Monitor contractor work against project requirements

steps.what: Gather contractor progress records and current plans schedules and budgets
Observe contractor and subcontractor work and clarify actual project progress
Compare work with specifications schedules and budgets and agree corrective follow-up

tasks.design: Configure a project reference view in {PROJECT} that links the current plans, budget, schedule and existing progress records. Reduce repeated collation while retaining site observation, conformance judgement and contractor discussion.
tasks.previous_blocker: Monitoring references are scattered across existing project records.
tasks.enabler_now: Native project views can collect links and current versions without generating a compliance judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Reported progress may differ from physical work or conceal quality issues.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising meaningful deviations and negotiating corrective action.
tasks.altitude: Less reference collation; no change to contractor oversight.

reach.task: Clarify whether observed changes affect approved project costs
reach.learn: How commitments differ from observed completion

evidence.claim: PlanRadar supports site diaries, checklists and defect reports, supporting the use of existing digital records as references rather than proving automated oversight.
The reference-view design and saving are unmeasured model assumptions.

assumptions: Boundary is manager monitoring; contractor work, existing reporting and cost-control work remain unchanged outside it.

Existing contractor leads produce dated progress records with project/work-package references through their current reporting; document control produces issue/revision/status and cost control produces the approved budget through unchanged work.
No new structured progress or discrepancy coding is demanded. s1 retains finding unmatched records, confirming versions and manual collation when links fail.
s2 retains physical observation and clarification; s3 retains all comparison and corrective agreement.
Test native project views first; no existing system runtime is counted as labour removed.
unknowns: Current record availability, version control and actual collation share
research_questions: Does a native reference view save collation time after checking currency and completeness?

already_counted.description: Reference selection and manual fallback in s1

incremental.description: Maintain reference views and investigate stale links

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=10+50+30=90; gross 10 minus 1 upkeep gives net 9. High needs usable existing records; low covers stale links and manual reference gathering. Contractor and cost-control effort is not credited.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Visit sites to establish solar requirements

steps.what: Travel to customer site and establish access for the visit
Discuss customer solar system needs and practical requirements
Survey site conditions to determine solar system requirements and specifications

tasks.design: Keep the visit, customer discussion and site survey with the manager. {DOCS} can hold existing survey information, but remote imagery or a generated summary is not assumed to establish actual installation conditions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements combine the customer's needs with physical site conditions.
tasks.enabler_now: No validated substitute for direct survey is established here.
tasks.still_hard: Conditions that need specialist assessment or cannot be established safely during the visit.
tasks.human_edge: Asking useful questions and recognising limitations of the survey.
tasks.altitude: No change to site survey responsibility.

reach.task: Translate checked survey findings into a suitable design
reach.learn: Which uncertain site details need further investigation

evidence.claim: The retained site visit and survey claim no software replacement or time saving.

assumptions: Boundary is visiting and establishing requirements, excluding design calculations and sales proposals.
s2 produces understood needs and s3 produces observed constraints; neither relies on an invented structured roof or customer requirement feed.
Existing visit arrangements are unchanged; no new customer data capture is transferred.
No new system or ongoing upkeep is introduced.
unknowns: Visit distance, site type and specialist survey requirements
research_questions: Is duplicate survey transcription a measured burden separate from visiting and observing?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=25+30+45=100. Travel, customer discussion and site survey retain their time, with zero incremental upkeep.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Purchase or rent solar installation equipment

steps.what: Assess installation equipment requirements site constraints and required dates
Compare suitable equipment offers and agree purchase or rental terms
Prepare check and submit authorised equipment purchase or rental order

tasks.design: Configure repeat-order fields in {PROCUREMENT} to reduce booking paperwork after the manager selects suitable equipment and terms. The manager checks and sends the exact purchase or rental order within existing authority; availability and equipment suitability remain human checks.
tasks.previous_blocker: Booking repeats supplier, project and delivery details after the substantive decision.
tasks.enabler_now: Native purchase forms can reuse existing records without selecting equipment autonomously.
tasks.still_hard: Equipment fit, access, genuine availability and rental exclusions.
tasks.human_edge: Understanding whether an offer meets actual site needs.
tasks.altitude: Less order entry; equipment selection and commitment authority stay unchanged.

reach.task: Clarify rental exclusions and purchase terms
reach.learn: Which conditions alter total cost and responsibility

evidence.claim: Reusing order fields can reduce booking administration while selection and supplier checks remain human; this is an unmeasured scenario.

assumptions: Boundary is manager equipment purchase/rental work, excluding supplier preparation and physical delivery.
s1 counts capture of equipment requirements, site access, dates and delivery location; s2 counts availability, price and terms obtained from the supplier and the manager's selection.
Existing buyer records produce supplier identity and standard terms through unchanged work; there is no assumed structured live availability feed.
s3 retains entry of selected terms, missing-field fallback and the exact-version check before sending. Revised offers need a fresh check.
Test native purchase forms first; no new supplier data capture or autonomous substitute selection is introduced.
unknowns: Purchase authority, native forms and repeat-order frequency
research_questions: Does repeat-field reuse save time after checking dates, delivery and rental conditions?

already_counted.description: Order completion and exact-version approval in s3

approvals.approved_version: Exact supplier, equipment specification, quantity, purchase/rental type, dates, delivery location, price and terms in the order; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=40+40+12=92; gross 8 minus 1 upkeep gives net 7. High needs repeat booking fields; low covers unusual equipment and changing terms consuming the benefit.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce request preparation and reference collation while retaining surveys and contractor judgement.
reach: Give inspectors, designers and buyers checked project context
role.ambitious_version: Coordinate solar projects using clear records and accountable human decisions.
